title: Android and Android-based Fire TV
lead: Use the Kotlin and Compose app to load HLS/DASH sources, try live rewind, and compare the shared Web UI. Android-based Fire TV and Vega OS are separate targets.

blocks.text: Preparation and build

Java 17 and the Android SDK are required. Player 3.171.0 requires compileSdk 37; the project uses AGP 9.1.1 and Gradle 9.3.1, with targetSdk 36 and minSdk 23. Install platform 37.0 (platforms;android-37.0) and Build Tools 36.0.0 (build-tools;36.0.0), matching CI. Set the SDK location with ANDROID_HOME, ANDROID_SDK_ROOT, or apps/android/local.properties. After synchronizing licenses and the shared UI in the common preparation, run the following from the repository root.

cd apps/android
./gradlew :app:assembleDebug

The output is apps/android/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk. You can also open apps/android in Android Studio and run on a connected device or emulator. Allow the application ID com.showcase.dvr on the Player license.

sync-env.sh transfers licenses from the root .env file to bitmovinLicenseKey and bitmovinAnalyticsLicenseKey in local.properties. The script preserves the local SDK path. Gradle’s -PbitmovinLicenseKey and -PbitmovinAnalyticsLicenseKey override local.properties, but the generated file is preferable for normal use to avoid leaving values in command history. An empty Analytics license disables the collector.
Suggested screen workflow

items: Use the source buttons to select Live DASH + DVR, Live HLS, Live DASH with multiple audio tracks or subtitles, VOD HLS, or VOD DASH. The first Live DASH + DVR source loads at startup.
Start playback with the controls inside the player. Switch between Default, Sports, Live (DVR), and Cinema to compare layouts and displays.
Use −10s, −30s, or −60s to seek to the specified distance behind the live edge. Use Live edge to return to live. Finite VOD, including a completed live source, disables these live commands.
Check Allow DVR, mode, dvrAvailable, behindLive, window, and the event log below. Scroll the button rows horizontally on a narrow screen and the whole panel vertically.
If PlayerError or SourceError appears, check its numeric code. First check the application ID allowed by the license and connectivity to the reference source.

blocks.text: Changing the Android UI recreates PlayerView while keeping the Player. This differs from iOS and React Native, which recreate the Player. The Sports, Live, and Cinema JavaScript and CSS load from file:///android_asset/. If the custom UI does not appear, build and synchronize the shared UI, then rebuild the APK. The Activity forwards start, resume, pause and stop to the active PlayerView. A replacement catches up to an already resumed Activity. The lifecycle observer is removed before detaching and destroying a retired view; the controller retains Player ownership across UI changes. In the recorded SDK 3.171.0 phone-emulator check, foregrounding kept playback paused; use the player’s Play control to resume when needed.

blocks.title: Checking TV devices
blocks.text: The Manifest declares LEANBACK_LAUNCHER for Android TV and Fire TV. Focus navigation, button reachability, remote controls, and actual playback still need testing on each device. A successful phone-emulator test does not establish behavior on physical devices or TVs.
Configuration drafts and applying changes

Open Configuration to edit 18 settings. Source fields are a custom HTTP/HTTPS URL, DASH/HLS/Smooth/Progressive type, optional title, optional poster URL, persistent poster, start offset in seconds, SDK-default/Start/End reference, and optional live target latency in seconds. Blank title, poster, and offset use SDK defaults. The default reference is the start for VOD and the end for live streams; the SDK corrects offsets outside stream boundaries. HTTP depends on the device network policy.

Live target latency maps to SourceLiveConfig.targetLatency. Blank keeps the original SDK defaults (liveConfig = null). An explicit finite value changes the SDK’s definition of the live edge and asks it to approach that latency while avoiding stalls; VOD ignores it. Apply source reloads the source, player recreation retains the applied value, and Reset source draft restores it without applying. This setting does not guarantee convergence within a deadline or establish stable return to the moving live edge.

Player fields are Autoplay (off), Start muted (off), SDK live time shifting (on), startup threshold (2.5 s), restart threshold (5 s), forward buffer (50 s), maximum automatic video bitrate (whole bps; blank means Int.MAX_VALUE / 2147483647, no ABR cap), preload (on), rebuffering (on), and live quality/stability balance (0–1; default 0.5). Thresholds must be nonnegative and at most forward buffer minus 0.5 s; forward buffer must be at least 0.5 s. Numeric fields reject non-finite values. The bitrate cap affects automatic selection; higher qualities remain available for manual selection. Balance applies near the live edge only.

items: Edit a draft, then choose Apply source (reload) to load it in the existing player. Invalid drafts leave the applied source and player unchanged.

Choose Apply & restart player for playback, buffer, or adaptation changes. It creates a new player with the current source and its metadata/options, keeping UI mode, Allow DVR, and the event log. Playback position resets according to the source start offset and autoplay settings.

Reset source draft returns to the applied source. Reset player draft restores SDK defaults. Neither button applies changes. Selecting any catalog preset, including the same one again, replaces the source draft and clears custom metadata, offsets, and live target latency.

blocks.text: Scroll the panel vertically to reach all fields. Existing source, UI, and seek rows still scroll horizontally; new editor choices and actions wrap on narrow screens. Controls stay within safe system-bar and cutout insets. Use directional keys to move focus; focused configuration switches show an outline.

Show applied code displays Kotlin PlayerConfig, SourceConfig and PlayerViewConfig for the applied settings and current UI, including optional live target latency. Draft edits are excluded. Copy code writes the text to the Android clipboard and shows Copied; license keys use placeholders. The example still needs the integrating app’s keys, view attachment and lifecycle forwarding.
Offline code example

OfflineManager is a helper around OfflineContentManager. It demonstrates retrieving download candidates, selecting the lowest-bitrate video and first audio track, downloading, and obtaining the resulting OfflineSourceConfig. It also includes calls for state, progress, deletion, and resource release.

MainActivity does not call this class, and there is no GUI for downloading, offline playback, or deletion. It is an integration example that needs to be connected to a screen, not a completed screen feature. In the integrating app, check the required service configuration, storage space, content and licenses, and actual playback with networking disabled. Successful compilation does not prove that downloading or offline playback works.
Running tests and reading recorded results

The full instrumented suite requires an authorized license and the local 60-second HLS/DASH finalization fixture. With Node 24, generate the local test media and start the server from the repository root. In a second terminal, forward ports 5272 and 5273 with adb reverse before running the tests below. Remove both forwards and stop the server afterwards. Only the debug build permits loopback HTTP for localhost and 127.0.0.1; release network policy is unchanged.

python3 encoding/test-streams/local.py
node apps/android/runtime-fixture.mjs .cache/test-streams/vod-baseline
# In another terminal:
adb reverse tcp:5272 tcp:5272
adb reverse tcp:5273 tcp:5273

blocks.title: Run from apps/android
blocks.text:
./gradlew :dvr:test :app:testDebugUnitTest
./gradlew :app:connectedDebugAndroidTest

The DVR JVM tests check rewind calculations. App JVM tests check draft validation, SDK mapping and lifecycle ownership, including catch-up for a resumed replacement and observer removal. Configuration instrumented tests drive the real editor and D-pad; recording ownership tests check exactly-once destroy calls and retired callback rejection. These checks do not establish media playback. Licensed tests check finite VOD duration, shared WebView controls, source switching, live seeking and configured autoplay/mute/start offset. The UI-handoff tests check 12 view replacements plus two real Activity stop/resume cycles, source/settings/UI/Allow DVR retention, explicit Play after foregrounding, viewport visibility, playback progress and Player invalidation through teardown. They do not establish completed release of all SDK resources.

The configured-start check captures the first TimeChanged after fresh Ready and RenderFirstFrame for the new player/source owner, including a zero sample. Its 9.0–13.0-second range and 40-second deadline are unchanged; Loaded and isPlaying can precede readiness. Standard UI checks verify Play/Pause/Mute/Unmute, seek, 1.5x speed and audio/subtitle/video-quality choices against native state or fresh events. A standard seek-bar hover reaches Player.getThumbnail and the active Source.getThumbnail delegation; the reference asset returns no image. On the tested phone, fullscreen/PiP handlers and visible buttons are absent and the mobile volume slider is hidden; these routes are verified unavailable. The code-view test checks applied/draft isolation, UI selection, feedback and exact real OS clipboard text.

HLS ENDLIST and DASH static tests retain the same URL, source and player through fresh PlaybackFinished at the finite media end, VOD/DVR-disabled state, visible Replay and replay-clock progress. They require fresh VOD seek completion, live controls hidden during Replay, visible live controls restored on a new live generation, and an explicit VOD switch. The SDK reports finite duration and isLive = false on this Android fixture; the app does not rewrite native getters.

Even when the shared UI exists, its control layout and auto-hide state can change later. The tests check ancestor visibility as well as display dimensions. Rewind completion must land within three seconds of a media target captured before the request; that tolerance is not a product guarantee. Return to live still requires a fresh completion event, an SDK offset within one second of zero, and visible LIVE text/button state. Failure reports record monotonic request/completion times, target and completion positions, offsets, native-ready poll counts, and live-control visibility; SDK error messages and configuration dumps are omitted.

The return check uses a fresh TimeShifted event, an SDK-reported timeShift within one second of zero, and genuinely visible LIVE text/button state within the same 40-second deadline. Native conditions are checked again after the UI result. Latency minus configured target latency is a separate diagnostic, not a promised sub-second synchronization SLA. Player 3.171.0 can report timeShift = 0 while that distance remains nonzero. Source.seekableRange returns (0, 0) for live sources, so its end is not a live media endpoint. Current time, raw latency, configured/effective target, buffers and range remain recorded. During time shifting, isStalled is false by definition; neither it nor an offset alone proves a completed seek. The optional policy retains the SDK catch-up/fallback rates of 1.2/0.95 and infinite seek thresholds; Player.playbackSpeed excludes temporary catch-up adjustments.

blocks.title: October 21 recorded verification scope
blocks.text: Player 3.171.0 passed 18 JVM tests (six DVR, ten configuration, two lifecycle) and app/instrumentation builds. The authorized Android 16/API 36.1 ARM64 phone-emulator group passed all 16 checks in 237.139 seconds, including configured VOD, strict LIVE, standard UI actions/availability, both finalization formats, real clipboard, 12 UI handoffs and two stop/resume cycles with explicit Play. Normal live return completed in 157 ms with +0.002 s fixed-target error; native zero offset and visible LIVE agreed 206 ms after the request. The configured VOD first position after fresh Ready/frame events was 10.256 s. Both finalization cases also passed a focused check of fresh VOD seek completion and visible live controls restored by a new load in 69.860 s. The optional 30-second latency policy passed the coupled return check under controlled emulator delay, without changing SDK defaults or adding seek retries. These runs do not promise seek-completion or latency-convergence timing. A previous close recorded timeout 1004 with no specific timed-out operation captured; this final group did not reproduce it or establish its resolution. Physical devices, Android TV, Fire TV, offline, casting, Analytics receipt and completed SDK resource cleanup are outside this scope.
